feedback.problem:
Calculate the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by $x=⟨1,2,3⟩$, $y=⟨0,1,-1⟩$, and $z=⟨2,0,1⟩.$

$V=${{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by three vectors is given by the absolute value of their triple product.

First, we compute the triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (y\times z) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|+3\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(1\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot 0)-2(0\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot 2)+3(0\cdot 0-1\cdot 2) \\  & =1-4-6 \\  & =-9\end{aligned}
$$

    

Finally, we take the absolute value. So, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped is 

$$
V=|-9|=9.
$$
